problem: The suite lacked a specialist that owns machine-readable API compatibility, provider conformance, and consumer/provider contract verification without collapsing those concerns into general testing or architecture.
triggers: OpenAPI or equivalent API contract changes
CI gate for versioned API compatibility

owns: provider conformance to a published contract
versioned contract fixtures and compatibility evidence

overlap_review: Distinct from testing-typescript-systems because this skill owns compatibility semantics and contract evidence; distinct from typescript-node-architecture because it verifies contracts rather than designing the broader architecture.
current_evidence: The skill has been created with static validation, routing coverage, and a representative behavioral case definition, but no controlled post-creation behavioral execution has tested whether loading this skill improves outcomes.

minimum_criteria: breaking response change is identified against a versioned contract/consumer expectation
schema validity is not confused with backward compatibility
provider/consumer verification evidence is distinguished from ordinary integration tests

limitations: unknown consumers can still break outside the recorded contract set
contract checks do not prove business semantics, authorization, performance, or production readiness
promotion_requirements: execute at least one controlled representative case after creation
show criterion-level value beyond general testing/architecture guidance
rejection_condition: Merge into testing-typescript-systems or retire if real use shows compatibility semantics are not independently useful.
